replies.author: @RealLifeExplorerUS
replies.text:
Cuba has faced a broad U.S. economic embargo for decades, which critics argue has added serious pressure to everyday life, while U.S. governments have said the sanctions are intended to pressure the Cuban government over political and human-rights issues.
Haiti’s situation is different: it is not currently under the same kind of broad U.S. economic embargo. The main international restrictions today include a UN arms embargo and targeted sanctions aimed at people and groups linked to gang violence and instability.

replies.author: @RealLifeExplorerUS
replies.text:
Cuba certainly has strong potential for ocean-based renewable energy, including wave and tidal power. The challenge is that these technologies can be expensive to develop and maintain, especially in harsh saltwater conditions, and they require significant investment, infrastructure, and specialized equipment.
Still, with Cuba’s long coastline, it’s an interesting possibility for the future.

comments.text:
The Cuban people will not surrender. They rose up and rejected Batista. They endured and persevered through Castro. And for over six decades—since 1962—they have survived the crushing weight of the U.S. embargo, bending but never breaking. Now, with the potential backing of BRICS, they may finally have the leverage to defeat the forces that seek to impose yet another Batista upon their shores.

Cubans are among the bravest and most resilient people on this planet. They have been starved, blockaded, and demonized, yet they refuse to kneel. Their spirit is unbroken, their resolve unshaken. History has tested them time and again—and each time, they have stood firm.
